name: Cult of the Damned
summary: Across Lordaeron, the Cult of the Damned still serves the Lich King. Before the Third War, its poisoned grain spread the Scourge and helped bring down humanity's greatest kingdom. Now cultists tend plague cauldrons and necromantic academies in the Plaguelands, while living agents infiltrate the cities of the living.

sections.title: A Sickness in the Soul
sections.body: Kel'Thuzad founded the cult after hearing the Lich King's whispers from the Frozen Throne. Exiled from the Kirin Tor, the archmage returned to Lordaeron with great wealth and forbidden arts. To the desperate poor, he promised equality and freedom from misery. To wealthy landowners such as House of Barov, he promised eternal life and lasting power over their domains. Both were drawn into a death cult meant to betray their homeland from within.

sections.title: The Poisoned Harvest
sections.body:
Beneath Caer Darrow, cultists practiced necromancy in secret. They built abominations and perfected the Plague of Undeath brought from Northrend. Then they contaminated grain stores in Andorhal, Lordaeron's breadbasket.

Flour traveled along merchant routes to homes across the Eastweald. Within days, commoners sickened and died, then rose as thralls under the Lich King's command. When Prince Arthas killed Kel'Thuzad in Andorhal, the cult had already spread too far to stop the kingdom's fall.

sections.title: The Present Threat
sections.body: The Cult of the Damned still threatens northern Lordaeron under the resurrected archlich Kel'Thuzad. Living cultists operate from the ruins of Stratholme and Scholomance. They perform dark rites, tend plague cauldrons among ruined farms, and try to kill Scarlet Crusaders and Forsaken. Their agents pass unnoticed through settlements, poison wells, disrupt supplies, and recruit others for the Scourge.

faq.q: Why would living mortals join a cult that turns people undead?
aliases: why join cult of the damned
faq.answer: Kel'Thuzad preyed on mortal weakness. He promised the poor equality and relief from hardship, while offering nobles such as Baron Rivendare and the Barov family immortality and lasting power. Many initiates did not learn the plague's true nature until escape was no longer possible.

faq.q: Why are cultists allowed to stay alive instead of being killed and raised?
faq.answer: Living agents can pass unnoticed through human settlements, trade along merchant routes, buy supplies, and undermine kingdoms from within. Cult doctrine treats undeath as a reward earned through devoted service.

faq.q: Where is the Cult of the Damned based?
faq.answer: The cult's chief spiritual and scholastic refuge is Scholomance, in the catacombs beneath Caer Darrow. Cultists also gather in Stratholme's ruins, around plague cauldrons in both Plaguelands, and in secret cells within living settlements.

faq.q: Who founded the Cult of the Damned?
faq.answer: Archmage Kel'Thuzad founded the cult after leaving the Kirin Tor in disgrace for forbidden necromancy. He traveled north, communed with the Lich King, gained great power, and returned to Lordaeron to organize the Scourge's mortal vanguard.

faq.q: How does the Cult of the Damned spread the plague today?
faq.answer: Cultists first spread the plague through tainted grain from Andorhal. Now they use great cauldrons across Plaguelands farms, where cauldron lords brew reagents that release blight and raise fallen corpses.

faq.q: What is the cult's relationship to the Forsaken?
faq.answer: The Forsaken and the cult are bitter enemies. The Forsaken broke free of the Lich King's command and seek vengeance on the Scourge. Cultists call them stolen property and heretics, and seek to destroy them or reclaim Lordaeron's ruins for the Frozen Throne.

angles.text: As a human, you remember Lordaeron's fall. The Cult of the Damned recalls how traitors within human cities and estates helped bring humanity down alongside demons.
As Forsaken, you know cultists as lapdogs who gave up their freedom to the master whose mental chains you fought to break.
As a paladin, you face a blasphemy against the Holy Light. Cultists use necromancy to corrupt the living and disturb the dead.
As a mage, you know the cult stains the Kirin Tor's honor. Kel'Thuzad, one of Dalaran's esteemed archmages, founded it.
As an Alliance soldier or scout, you must watch for cult infiltrators seeking to spread plague and chaos in living cities such as Stormwind.
